transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-06-30
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Claire Brooks (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (VeloxSearch Head of Search), Diego Morales (VeloxSearch Lead ML Eng), Priya Rao (VeloxSearch CTO)

Summary: quick hosted API demo focused on embeddings + rerank workflow for search relevance. Showed embedding generation, similarity search, and Redwood's rerank endpoint with API + console metrics. Discussed costs/tradeoffs and security requirements. Agreed on PoC next steps.

---
00:00 Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm samir with redwood, and with me is claire who will do most of the tech walkthrough. can you do quick intros?
00:15 Laura: hi i'm laura, head of search at velox, we own relevance across web+docs.
00:19 Diego: diego here, lead ml eng, i'll own the integration and the evaluation.
00:23 Priya: priya, cto, curious about infra and compliance impact.
00:28 Claire: great, thanks — i want to set expectations, we'll show hosted embeddings, a simple similarity flow, then our rerank endpoint which can take the top-k and reorder using context; also console views and optimize recs.

01:05 Claire: so first slide — hosted embeddings api, single REST call, or python sdk. example: POST /v1/embeddings with model=redwood-embed-1, input=[...]. returns vectors, we also handle batched inputs, and have builtin normalization.
01:25 Diego: how big are the vectors typically? 1536? 1024?
01:29 Claire: currently we have 1024 and 1536 options depending on model family; for search we normally recommend 1536 for doc-level, 1024 for sentence-level.
01:40 Samir: note on billing: embeddings billed per unit, and batch sizes affect throughput/cost — we can show optimize suggestions for batching later.

03:12 Claire: live demo time — i'm going to paste a short python snippet. (typing noises)
03:18 Claire: "from redwood import Client; c=Client(api_key='***'); r = c.embeddings.create(model='redwood-embed-1', input=['what is redwood inference?', 'velox feature doc']);" — returns list of vectors.
03:35 Laura: is there an async streaming option for embeddings?
03:38 Claire: embeddings are synchronous call today; generation streaming applies to text gen. but we can process large batches and we recommend chunked uploads.

05:00 Claire: next step, similarity search — typical flow: index vectors in your vector DB (we integrate w/ pinecone, milvus, etc) and do top-k retrieval. then you call our rerank endpoint to re-order top-k using the model's context scoring.
05:20 Diego: why use rerank vs just cosine similarity?
05:23 Claire: good q — cosine is fast and good for initial recall, rerank uses cross-encoder style scoring with full context+query and tends to improve click-through by surfacing more relevant results, especially for tricky queries and long docs. cost is higher per item since it scores pairs, so it's top-k only.

07:45 Claire: i'll demo the rerank API: POST /v1/rerank with payload: {"model": "redwood-rerank-1", "query": "how to set up sso", "candidates": ["doc1","doc2",...]} returns scores and reordered ids. (note: transcription may have braces munged)
07:58 Diego: can it accept embeddings as candidates (i.e., vector + id) to avoid re-fetching doc text?
08:05 Claire: currently rerank expects text candidates; we're working on a hybrid path that accepts embeddings+ids to reduce data movement but for now we fetch the snippet. some customers prefetch small snippets to speed it up.

09:30 Samir: important tradeoff — latency. if you rerank top 10 you'll add ~50-150ms depending on model/seq length; we show live console numbers.
09:42 Claire: switching to console — here's per-route latency, token-level cost, and token breakdown. you can set SLOs and have fallback policies: if rerank times out, we fall back to cosine-only ordering.
10:05 Laura: can we see an example of the fallback?
10:08 Claire: sure — in the config panel you can choose fallback: "cosine", "previous-deployed-model", or "no-fallback". we'll demo timeout at 200ms and then show cos fallback. (demo click)

12:00 Claire: now i'll run a quick benchmark on a small query set — comparing recall with cosine-only vs cosine+rerank. (typing) results: avg MRR up 12% on our sample, precision@5 up 9%, latency for rerank route avg 120ms.
12:30 Priya: that delta is interesting; what about cost per query?
12:33 Samir: typical per-query cost moves from $0.002 (cosine only + embed retrieval) to ~ $0.007-$0.01 with rerank at top10 depending on model size. Optimize module can recommend quantized model variants and batching to reduce that.

14:10 Claire: speaking of optimize, here's the Optimize tab — suggestions show: increase batching to 16 for embeddings during bulk indexing, use a 16-bit quantized variant for rerank in low-latency mode, and enable KV prefix caching for repeated context to shave off tokens.
14:35 Diego: prefix caching — does that work cross-tenant?
14:38 Claire: caching is per-customer and per-model; KV cache stores decoder state for generation; for rerank it can reduce repeated context encoding if queries share doc snippets. it's configurable.

16:00 Priya: security questions — SOC2? audit logs? kms?
16:05 Samir: yes we are SOC2 Type II; we provide audit logs via console and can integrate with customer SIEM. for private deployments we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations.
16:20 Priya: data residency — we need EU-only processing for some datasets.
16:25 Claire: hosted EU regions are available; for strict residency we recommend Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) which gives full control. we can map the PoC scope and data needs.

18:10 Laura: any SSO / SAML support for RBAC?
18:12 Samir: yes SAML and OIDC SSO with SCIM provisioning; RBAC roles in console, and per-route API keys if you want fine-grained access.

20:00 Diego: technical detail — if we choose hosted, how do we do A/B rollouts for rerank models?
20:05 Claire: console supports canary / A-B split with traffic weights, and automatic fallback based on latency thresholds or quality regressions. we also have an eval harness so you can run held-out queries to compare metrics before rolling.

22:30 Claire: quick note about integration: typical PoC steps — 1) small index of ~10k docs, 2) run baseline sim search + rerank on holdout set, 3) measure MRR / precision and query latency, 4) tune batching and quantization.
22:50 Diego: we have a 25k doc dataset and a 2k query set, should be fine for PoC.

24:15 Laura: what about vendor lock? if we index vectors to pinecone and then want to move, how tied are we to redwood?
24:22 Samir: you control vector storage; Redwood only serves embeddings and rerank scoring — you can always move vectors, and we support export. we also provide model-variant compatibility info so you can replicate scoring outside with an open model if desired.

27:00 Priya: question about on-prem pricing model — is there a license + infra or per-token?
27:05 Samir: Private has platform fee + support tier and then usage/instance pricing depending on reserved capacity; we'll send detailed pricing.

29:10 Claire: back to demo — showing a snippet of the rerank response, it returns candidates with scores and an optional explainability payload (highlights may be noisy in transcription).
29:28 Diego: can we get logits or just normalized scores?
29:31 Claire: we return normalized scores by default, and can expose raw logits for debugging in private deployments or with support agreement.

32:00 Samir: ok i'm going to recap and propose next steps. agreed PoC scope is: run on velox's 25k docs, use 2k query eval, compare cosine-only vs cosine+rerank top10, target metric MRR + latency tradeoff.
32:20 Laura: yes that's accurate. timeline?
32:23 Samir: Claire and i will share a benchmark spreadsheet and PoC playbook by Friday (2028-07-05). we'll follow up with security whitepaper and SOC2 cert link. Diego to share sample data and infra contacts by 2028-07-06.

34:00 Priya: one last ops question — will we need network peering or any special egress setup for hosted?
34:05 Claire: for hosted it's standard HTTPS egress; for lower-latency or compliance heavy workloads we can do Private with peering or on-prem. we'll note that in the PoC doc.

36:40 Laura: any blockers from our side? i think infra can allocate a spot instance for initial indexing.
36:45 Diego: i'll coordinate, no blockers.

38:10 Samir: great, thanks everyone. we'll send the materials and book the PoC kickoff — any other questions?
38:18 Priya: none from me.
38:20 Laura: nope, thanks for the clear demo.

39:00 Claire: (wrap) note: small transcription glitches possible; full recording + slides + benchmark sheet will be attached to the follow-up.

Action recap:
- Samir to send pricing + PoC guide (due 2028-07-03)
- Claire to share benchmark spreadsheet + security whitepaper (due 2028-07-05)
- Diego to provide sample dataset and query set (due 2028-07-06)
